**Finding submitted: compliant (at the fallback).** No redline proposed.

**Summary of the review**

| Fallback element | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Commitment limited to current 12-month term | § 13 (p0078) — 1-year term, one-year renewals, 30-day non-renewal right for either party |
| Reducible / exitable on ~30 days' notice | § 14 (p0079) — Client's at-will termination; minimum stops end of the month following notice |
| True-up, not a penalty | No shortfall, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums anywhere in the document |

The minimum in § 5(a) is a real take-or-pay-style floor on us, so this isn't the preferred position — but because it can't outlive the current 12-month term and we hold a unilateral exit that switches it off on roughly a month's notice with no recapture, it meets the fallback on every material term and the playbook says not to redline it.

Two things I flagged in the rationale rather than as deviations, both worth picking up in the commercial pass:

1. **The dollar figures are blank.** `$____ per month` for both Hosting and Support. The classification holds only because the exit works; the actual exposure is unknown until those blanks are filled. They should be set against realistic baseline usage before signature — this is the single highest-value negotiation point left on the clause.
2. **§ 6 (p0047) carves the minimum fees out of our documentation and dispute rights.** We can't demand backup for, or contest, precisely the amounts we're committed to pay. That belongs under the audit/disputes rule, so I left it there rather than double-flagging the same commercial term.

I also checked and deliberately did **not** flag the "not less than ____ months" programmer-availability undertaking in § 4 (p0043) — that is a commitment TrueLink makes to us and runs in our favour. Similarly, the storage and bandwidth allotments in § 3 are service specifications, not volume caps on our usage. One drafting oddity noted in passing: the internal numbering is offset from the section headings, so § 6's reference to "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" actually points at Support Services rather than Compensation, and § 2(c) and § 13 cross-refer to "Section 12" for termination when the termination provision is § 14.
